title: the Ninth Floor Rising
premise: Oscar Coldharbour, an obsessive urban explorer who maps the unmapped tunnels beneath the city of Vell, is hired to survey a construction site where a crew has unearthed a door sealed from the inside. Behind it lies the Ninth Floor, a subterranean level erased from every record by the city's founders, who bound something there with a ritual that requires a living mapmaker's memory as its lock. As Oscar descends, she discovers her own childhood blackout was a previous visitation, and that the founders' descendants have been feeding explorers to the Floor for generations. To survive and seal it properly, Oscar must complete the ritual by surrendering her memories of everyone she loves — and in the end she does, walking out alive but unable to remember why the tunnels ever mattered, while the thing below keeps a perfect record of everything she gave away.
about_author: Jonah Kavanagh is the pen name of a former municipal archivist who spent six years cataloguing condemned buildings before turning to horror full-time. They live above a decommissioned subway line and claim they can no longer hear the trains.

chapters.title: The Survey
chapters.summary: Oscar Coldharbour, POV. Oscar takes a contract to map the Vell Foundry excavation site, establishing her rituals: counted doors, marked lights, annotated maps. The crew unearths a steel door bolted shut from within, warm to the touch. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into fascination as Oscar realizes the door matches a shape from her own childhood nightmares.

chapters.title: Sealed From Inside
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Against protocol, Oscar examines the door alone at night and finds scratch marks on the inner face spelling her surname. A foreman disappears; the crew refuses to return. The site owner, Marguerite Vell, hires Oscar back at triple pay, revealing she knows more than she says. Emotional beat: dread mixed with the flattery of being chosen.

chapters.title: What the Founders Buried
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV, intercut with archival fragments. In the city records office, Oscar finds the Ninth Floor deliberately excised from blueprints, its founders' portraits defaced. She learns the ritual: a map drawn in memory, renewed each generation by someone who can hold the Floor in their mind without going mad. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery shadowed by the realization she was recruited, not hired.

chapters.title: The Door Opens
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. The door unseals itself during a blackout; the darkness inside counts her footsteps back to her. Oscar descends against every instinct, finding corridors that rearrange when unobserved and rooms furnished like her childhood home. She encounters a previous explorer, hollow-eyed and repeating door numbers. Emotional beat: terror tempered by the compulsion to keep mapping.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Confession
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Oscar above ground, Marguerite below via found letters. Marguerite admits the Vell family has fed the Floor a mapmaker every forty years, and Oscar's childhood disappearance near the tunnels means she was already marked. The Floor doesn't want her body; it wants her memory, the only material that can rebuild its walls. Emotional beat: betrayal and the sick relief of finally understanding.

chapters.title: Rooms That Remember
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Descending deeper, Oscar passes rooms staging scenes from her past: her mother's kitchen, a hospital corridor, the day of her blackout. Each room costs her a memory to walk through, and she begins leaving herself notes she later cannot read. She finds the founders' ritual chamber, half-finished, waiting for a final hand. Emotional beat: grief for memories still being lost.

chapters.title: The Hollow Cartographer
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Oscar meets the last mapmaker, Aldous Vell, kept alive for eighty years as the Floor's failing lock, his mind scraped blank. He begs her to finish the ritual or release him. The Floor offers Oscar a bargain: walk away and let it rise into the city, or stay and become its new wall. Emotional beat: rage at the cruelty of a choice with no clean exit.

chapters.title: Counting Doors
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. The Floor floods upward toward the excavation crew and the streets above; doors appear throughout Vell, all opening inward. Oscar races through shifting corridors using her mapping discipline as a weapon, counting, annotating, refusing to forget on purpose. She reaches the ritual chamber as the city above begins to remember the Ninth Floor exists. Emotional beat: desperate clarity — her obsession is the one tool the Floor cannot digest.

chapters.title: The Ninth Ritual
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV. Climax. Oscar completes the founders' rite, drawing the Floor's true geometry from memory onto its own walls, binding it — but the ritual demands payment in kind. She chooses which memories to feed it, sacrificing her mother's face, her first love, the reason she explores at all. Aldous dies free as the new lock takes hold. Emotional beat: triumphant devastation.

chapters.title: Lights On, Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Oscar, POV, epilogue weeks later. Oscar walks out of the site alive; the door is gone, the crew remembers nothing, and Marguerite pays her in silence. Oscar resumes exploring, keeping her lights on and her doors counted, though she no longer knows why the habit matters. On her wall, a map appears in her handwriting of tunnels she's never surveyed. Emotional beat: quiet, unresolved survival — the price paid, the debt not closed.
